- **Updates with your own mods folder.** If you point Fabric at a mods folder of its own with the Java argument `-Dfabric.modsFolder=...` (one game folder with a mods folder per Minecraft version, for example), **Updates** set to **Install** now installs the new version into that folder. Before, it only told you a new version was out. On Linux, Mac and Windows.
- **Pressing play with Spotify Web.** With Spotify Web, when you press play on a paused song, jump to another spot in a paused song or start a song from the song library, the lyrics and the top bar now catch up within about a second. Before, they could stand still (or say nothing is playing) for up to 4 seconds while the music already played: Spotify often still gives the old state for a moment after a press, and SkyLyrics then went back to asking it only every 4 seconds.
- **"Nothing playing" with Spotify Web.** With Spotify Web, the **Now playing** card on the Music tab now says "Play a song in Spotify on any device" while nothing plays, instead of suggesting a browser or any player: Spotify Web only follows your Spotify account, so a video in a browser or another music player never shows there.
- **Play/pause right after using your phone.** With Spotify Web, the play/pause key and button now work the first time after you paused or resumed Spotify somewhere else (your phone, the Spotify app). Before, a press a few seconds after that (up to 15 seconds with the lyrics off) could ask Spotify for what it was already doing, so nothing happened until you pressed again.
- **World words in a narrow window.** In the World layout, words no longer come up off the left or right edge of a tall or square window (a window tiled to half the screen, 800x1000) or at a low FOV: the scattered words and a **Flowing line**'s rows now keep to the width the screen really shows, where before they were spread as if every screen were 16:9. Wide screens show the words where they always did.
- **Quitting while a song plays.** Closing the game while SkyLyrics is reading your music player no longer writes "Couldn't read the music player" into the game's log, and a song change read in that last moment no longer sets off a lyrics and cover lookup that the closing game refuses (more lines in the log). It was likeliest on a Mac, where each read takes longest.
- **The song title after joining a world.** In the World layout, the song's name now floats up once the world shows, for its full few seconds. Before, it was put up while the loading screen still covered the world, so after a slow load (a busy server) it was half over or already gone when you could see.
- **World words by a wall or a hillside.** In the World layout, standing next to a wall, a cliff or a hillside no longer sends the words up its side one above the other, piled onto each other and off the top of the screen. A word with no clear place in front of the blocks is still lifted out of them, but only as high as the screen shows (for a **Flowing line**, no higher than its rows go, floating up counted) and only onto clear sky; otherwise it keeps its own place in the line, drawn through the blocks (or hidden behind them with **See through blocks** off).
- **Keyboard pick after a resize.** In the song library (grid and shelf) and in the settings, the card or row you picked with the keyboard now scrolls back into view when the window changes size (fewer columns or a shorter panel can move it out of sight), instead of staying hidden until the next key. If you scrolled with the mouse last, the list stays where you left it.
- **Bottom bar and F3's charts.** With **Bar position** on Bottom, F3's charts along the bottom of the screen (the profiler's pie, the frame time and network charts, and on 26.1 and later the light map) now hide the bar while they reach it, instead of being drawn over it. They reach it on screens up to about 830 wide in GUI units, like 1920x1080 at GUI scale 3 or 1280x720 at GUI scale 2; on wider screens they stay beside the bar and the bar stays.
- **Record card at the bottom and F3's charts.** With the **Record card** in a bottom corner, F3's charts along the bottom of the screen (the frame time or network chart on the left; the tick time or ping chart, the profiler's pie and on 26.1 and later the light map on the right) now hide the card while they reach it, instead of being drawn over it.
- **The note for a song without a cover.** The ♪ the top bar shows in place of a missing album cover no longer looks uneven (some of its strokes wider than others) with Minecraft's letters: like the Record card's small text, it is drawn at the nearest size where every pixel of it is the same width, so at GUI scale 2 and 3 it is a little bigger than before and at GUI scale 4 a little smaller.
- **Lyrics lines stamped before the start.** A line in a lyrics file stamped before the song starts (a minus in front, like `[-00:01.00]`, which some editors write after moving a whole file earlier) was left out, so the song began without its first words. It now shows from the very start, and a word timing stamped the same way in a file timed word by word (like `<-00:00.50>`) no longer shows in the sky with the words. A line stamped this way in full-width brackets (like `［-00:01.00］`, as some Chinese and Japanese lyrics write their stamps) shows from the start too, instead of being left out.
- **World layout and seeking.** Jumping back a moment with the mod's progress bar (half a second is enough) now takes the World layout's words back too, and the line being sung places its words again from the new spot. A jump back made in the music player itself counts from 1.5 seconds as before, so a player that reports its position a little late never wipes the words in the middle of a song.
- **Hide in caves high up.** With **Hide in caves** on, flying or teleporting higher than y 2048 no longer hides the lyrics, the top bar, the **Record card** and the night sky as if you had gone underground.
- **Debug lines set to show always.** On 1.21.9 and later, where the debug options screen (F3 + F6) can set any of F3's lines to show always, even with F3 closed (its Performance profile does this for the FPS line), the top bar and a **Record card** in a top corner now move down below those lines instead of being drawn under them: a top left card sat under a pinned FPS line (unless the top bar already kept it lower), and a top right card and the top bar's stats under the pinned system lines (at 1920x1080 and GUI scale 3). A bottom bar or a bottom card that pinned lines reach hides as it does for F3's text, and when so many lines are pinned that they run past the top third of the screen, the top bar and a top card hide as they do for F3. This holds steadily even at a very low frame rate (about 4 frames a second or less).
- **Snapshots and pre-releases.** The jar for 1.21.6 to 1.21.8 no longer says it works on the 1.21.9 snapshots, pre-releases and release candidates, and the jar for 26.1 no longer says it works on the 26.2 ones. On those the game crashed while loading SkyLyrics; now Fabric says which Minecraft versions the jar is for.
- **Spotify's own sign-in errors.** While Spotify's sign-in page is open, the Music tab now says what to check if Spotify shows INVALID_CLIENT: the Client ID, and that your Spotify app has the Redirect URI exactly as shown. Before, a wrong Client ID or a missing or mistyped Redirect URI left it at "Waiting for your browser…" until the sign-in timed out five minutes later.
- **Pasting the Client ID.** A Client ID copied with quotes, a label like "Client ID:" or a web page's spaces around it, or inside the address of its page on the Spotify dashboard, is now picked out when you press **Paste**, instead of showing "That isn't a Client ID".
- **Browsing the song library for hours.** On 1.21.4 and 1.21.5, every album cover the song library showed left a little memory behind until the game closed, so browsing for an evening slowly added to the game's memory use. Covers now reuse the room of the ones that scrolled away, so the memory they take stays the same however long you browse.
- **Font packs turned on from the title screen.** A resource pack that changes the width of only some letters (Cyrillic ones, say), turned on or off in the title screen's Options while a song plays, no longer leaves the title screen's lyrics drawn with the old letter widths: lines already shown kept their old line breaks and letter places (letters on top of each other or gaps inside words) for the rest of the song. Every resource reload now has every line laid out again.
- **Settings file nested very deep.** On Minecraft 1.21.1 to 1.21.10, a settings file with a value buried thousands of brackets deep (damaged, or made to break things) no longer crashes the game at every start or stops your settings from saving: the file or that setting counts as damaged and goes back to the default, as on the newer versions. The update check reads GitHub's answer the same careful way: one nested that deep now counts as no update, instead of ending the check with a long error in the game log.
- **Instrumentals named "(Inst.)".** A sung song whose release also has its instrumental as "Song (Inst.)" (common for K-pop and J-pop), or as "(伴奏)", "(纯音乐)", "(カラオケ)", "(オフボーカル)" or "(インスト)" on the NetEase backup, no longer shows as instrumental (or stays that way without ever asking the backup for its lyrics), and the instrumental no longer gets the sung song's lyrics.
- **Instrumental videos.** A video or file titled like "Song (Official Instrumental)", "Song (Instrumental Audio)" or "Song [Karaoke Video]" no longer gets the sung song's lyrics: the words "Official", "Audio" and "Video" still go, but "Instrumental" or "Karaoke" stays, so a browser now shows it as "Song (Instrumental)" (a timing you saved for one of these videos has to be set again).
- **Nothing looked up while Lyrics is off.** With **Lyrics** turned off, the mod no longer sends each new song's title, artist, album and length to the lyrics sites (LRCLIB, and NetEase as the backup), and no longer downloads its album cover; the **Music** tab's Lyrics row says "Lyrics off" meanwhile, its **Now playing** card shows no cover for that song (not the last song's), and **Retry** waits until **Lyrics** is on and then asks the lyrics sites again. Turning **Lyrics** back on looks up the song playing then.
- **Your name in the game log.** When the Spotify sign-in file can't be read, saved or removed (for example while Windows, an antivirus or OneDrive holds it) or Windows can't make it readable by you alone, or the Windows music reader can't be set up in the game folder, the line in the game log no longer shows your home folder, which on Windows carries your user name.
- **The search key with the Narrator on a Mac.** On a Mac, the Narrator's hint in the settings now says Cmd+F opens the search, instead of Ctrl+F, which does nothing there.
- **Update pop-up in your language.** The pop-up and chat line saying a new SkyLyrics is out or downloaded could be all in English when the game is set to another language: the update check is often done in a second or two, before the loading screen has loaded your language. They now wait for the loading screen to end.
- **Updates in packwiz modpacks.** In a modpack kept up to date by packwiz (its installer runs each time you press Play in Prism, MultiMC or ATLauncher), a SkyLyrics that came with the pack no longer installs its own update: the pack's installer would download the old jar again at the next launch, leaving two SkyLyrics in your mods folder. The mod now only tells you a new version is out, and the pack's maker updates it. A SkyLyrics you added to such a pack yourself still updates itself.
- **A proxy that asks for a password.** On a work or school network whose proxy wants a password, the **Music** tab no longer says "No lyrics found for this song" and stops asking: it says the lyrics sites can't be reached and keeps trying, so the lyrics come as soon as the proxy lets SkyLyrics through. Nothing is saved for the song meanwhile. Album covers are tried again too, instead of staying missing for that song (or, in the song library, for the rest of the game).
- **Spotify answers that stop halfway.** With Spotify signed in, an answer from Spotify that stops halfway (hotel Wi-Fi dropping for a moment, a phone hotspot or a proxy stalling) is now given up after 20 seconds and asked again, with "Can't reach the internet or Spotify" meanwhile. Before, the lyrics could stay on that song and play, pause and skip did nothing until you restarted the game.
- **The carousel with a trackpad.** In the song library's carousel, a small swipe on a Mac trackpad or a turn of a smooth (free-spinning) mouse wheel no longer races through dozens of covers: it moves one cover for each notch's worth of scrolling, as the hotbar does. A normal mouse wheel still moves one cover a notch.
- **Ctrl+click on a Mac.** On a Mac, Ctrl+click (the Mac's right click) in the settings and the song library no longer acts as a normal click a moment later: it no longer flips a switch, moves a slider or plays a song. Like a right click, it does nothing there.
- **Double-clicking "‹ Playlists".** In the song library, double-clicking "‹ Playlists" in an open playlist now takes you back to your playlists. Before, the second click landed on the Search or Liked songs tab that appears in the button's place.
- **Double-clicking Reset all.** In the settings, a double-click on **Reset all** no longer resets every setting at once: it asks "Click again to reset" as a single click does, and only a click of its own after that resets.
- **Sideways scrolling in the song library.** The shelf and the carousel, which run sideways, now also move with a sideways scroll: a trackpad swiped left or right, a mouse wheel that tilts, or Shift and the wheel on a Mac. Before, only scrolling up and down moved them.
- **Scrolling the shelf under the mouse.** In the song library's shelf, scrolling with the mouse resting on the covers now chooses the cover that slides under it, so the name shown is the one a click plays. Before, the name of the cover the mouse was on before the scroll stayed, while a click played the new one.
- **Clock in the game's language.** The top bar's clock now follows the language you play Minecraft in, not your computer's: in German, French, Russian, Ukrainian, Hebrew, Portuguese or the Spanish of Spain it shows 24 hours ("21:07") even on a computer set to American English, where it said "9:07 PM". Each language writes the time its own way (Canadian French "21 h 07"). In American English, the game's default, the clock still follows your computer, and so it does in Pirate Speak, Upside Down English, LOLCAT, Klingon and the game's other made-up languages, which say nothing about how you read the time. So it does in a language a resource pack adds under a code that names no real language.
- **Decimal commas.** In German, French, Russian, Ukrainian, Portuguese and Spanish (but not Mexican Spanish), the settings' numbers now have a decimal comma like the rest of the text: **Size** reads "1,25×", **Timing** "+0,25 s", **Linger** "1,2 s" and the Floating **Distance** "10,7 blocks", and so does the message above the hotbar when you press a timing key. English (Pirate Speak too), Swiss German, Mexican Spanish and Hebrew keep the point.
- **Top bar highlight in light colours.** With a light accent colour on the top bar (any of the colours to pick, a pale album colour with **Accent colour** set to **Album**, or the lyrics colour with **Lyrics**), the two sung words on the highlight were white on almost white and hard to read. The highlight now turns a deeper shade of that colour, just enough for the words to stand out. The default violet looks as before.
- **Top bar clock and FPS on a bright sky.** The clock and the frame rate beside the top bar now have the game's text shadow, like its own words over the world, so they no longer vanish against a bright sky, clouds or snow.
- **Record card's lines before and after.** With **Card lines** at **3 lines**, the lines before and after the one being sung were faded so far on the **Record card** that they were hard to make out. They are now just a little dimmer than the artist's name.
- **Record card in deep blue album colours.** With the lyrics in the album's colour, a deep blue or violet album no longer leaves the line being sung on the **Record card** too dark to read on the dark card: there it is lightened just enough to stand out (the lyrics in the sky keep the album's colour).
- **"Nothing playing" hint.** On the Music tab, when nothing plays, the line under "Nothing playing" on the **Now playing** card that says where to play a song now shows in full in a tooltip when you point at the card, if it ends in "…". In most languages it is too long for the card and was cut off with no way to read the rest. The Narrator now says that line too when the keyboard is on the card, instead of only "Nothing playing".
- **Signing out of Spotify.** Clicking **Sign out** on the Music tab no longer makes the game pause while the saved sign-in is removed (it could on a slow or network drive, or a game folder OneDrive keeps). Signing out just before you quit still leaves the next game signed out, also when Spotify had just renewed the sign-in and it was still being saved.
- **Hide in the Nether and the End on servers.** **Hide in the Nether** and **Hide in the End** now also work in the extra Nether and End worlds many servers make (a resource Nether, or worlds made with Multiverse on Paper and Spigot), and in a data pack's or mod's world of the Nether's or the End's kind. Before, the lyrics, the top bar and the **Record card** stayed up there, because only the main Nether and End counted.
- **Key messages and pop-ups with the Narrator.** The Narrator now reads what SkyLyrics writes above the hotbar when you press one of its keys (lyrics on or off, a song's timing, the view lock) and its pop-up and line in chat about a new version, as Minecraft does with its own messages. Before, it said nothing, so a player who can't see them didn't know the key had worked.
- **Fewer flashes from World words.** In the World layout, the white flash a word lands with and the one a word gets when you hit it now start at most three times a second, like the lyrics' other flashes. A fast line (more than three words a second) flashed every word, and clicking quickly at a word flashed it on every click, which can be too much for players sensitive to flashing light. The words in between now land in their own colour, and a word hit again soon after keeps fading from its last flash (it is still knocked away).
- **Song name and Notification Time.** The song's name after a song change now stays up as long as Minecraft's **Notification Time** (Accessibility settings) says, like Minecraft's own pop-ups: on the top bar (at the default, 3.5 seconds before it moves on to the line being sung, or 6 seconds before the bar hides with **Song name only on change**) and as the title in the World layout (4 seconds). Before, it stayed the same time whatever the setting said, too short for players who need longer to read.
- **Album covers in odd picture formats.** An album cover is whatever picture your music app hands over (one inside a song file, a podcast's or a radio station's), and one in a picture format album covers don't come in is no longer opened: a small file of that kind could make the game set aside a great deal of memory at once, enough to stall or even crash it. Covers in the usual formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF and BMP) show as before.
- **Album covers that took ages to load.** A specially made album cover picture can no longer keep your computer busy for minutes, or hours, while it loads, with no other covers loading meanwhile: it now takes no longer than an ordinary cover of its size.
- **iTunes and foobar2000 on Windows.** Where SkyLyrics names the player (the Music tab's **Status** line, "Following …", and the bar for a song with no artist), these two are now spelled their own way, "iTunes" and "foobar2000", instead of "Itunes" and "Foobar2000".
- **Rainbow colour on a computer that stays on.** The **Rainbow** colour and the Rainbow tile under **Themes** now flow smoothly however long the computer has been on since it was last restarted. Before, the colour changed in small jumps instead of every frame after a few days: after a month, five jumps a second on the lyrics and bigger, coarser ones on the tile.
- **Sky and hat errors on 1.21.9 and newer.** On Minecraft 1.21.9 and newer, a SkyLyrics error while drawing the sky effects or your hat no longer ends the game: that effect pauses for a few seconds and the error is written to the game log once, as on older versions.
- **Errors in the settings, the song library and the tour.** An error in one of the mod's screens (while it is drawn, read out by the Narrator, or when you press a key or click) no longer closes Minecraft with a crash report. The screen goes back to the one you opened it from, a pop-up says "Something went wrong, try again", and the error is written to the game log. When the error comes from a screen it opened (Minecraft's Controls, say), that screen stays, and the settings or the library show as usual when you go back to them. A tour that hit an error doesn't open again over the title screen until you restart the game.
- **Settings sliders set between two steps.** A slider whose value sits between two of its steps (written by hand in the settings file, or in one copied from another computer) now goes to the step right beside it with the Left and Right arrow keys. Before, one of the arrows skipped that step: **Timing** at +0.12 s went left to +0.05 s, and at +0.13 s right to +0.20 s.
- **Double-clicking All settings.** A double-click on **All settings** at the end of the welcome tour (or on another button that brings the settings up) no longer changes the setting under the mouse in the settings it opens. The second click landed there, and a click anywhere on a switch's row flips it: with the Arc or Lines layout picked, it could turn on **Lazy follow**.
- **Holding Enter on Reset all.** Holding Enter or Space a little long on **Reset all** in the settings no longer resets every setting by itself. The first press asks to be pressed again, and the repeats your computer sends while a key is held down counted as that second press. Holding the key that leaves the **Preview** no longer hides and shows it over and over, and holding Esc there no longer closes the settings too.

### Faster

- **No hitch when a setting changes.** Settings are saved in the background, so pressing a timing key or closing the settings no longer makes the game pause for a moment while the file is written (most noticeable on Windows when an antivirus or OneDrive holds the file). A change made right before you quit is still saved.
- **Smaller saved album covers.** Album covers are saved as small 128-pixel pictures, so they load faster and take less disk space. Big album covers saved by an older version are made small the next time they show, so an old cover folder shrinks as you play those songs again.
- **Lighter in the background.** On a Mac, while the lyrics are switched off and no SkyLyrics screen is open, the mod checks Spotify or Music about every 15 seconds instead of every second; it checks at once when you switch the lyrics back on. On Windows, while the lyrics are switched off and no SkyLyrics screen is open, the mod asks Windows for the song about every 15 seconds instead of every half second; it asks at once when you switch the lyrics back on.
- **Long lines in World, sparkles, faint glow.** A long line in the World layout (a fast rap verse) is measured once when it starts instead of once per letter, which could stall that frame. Sparkles that are out of view are no longer drawn, and a faint glow in the Arc layout uses the same lighter drawing the Lines layout already did.
- **Lighter lyrics and sky effects.** Lines and Arc lyrics and the Galaxy sky do less work each frame. The default Aurora sky, the Nebula clouds and stars, and the constellations skip the parts behind you or off the side of the screen. They look the same and cost less each frame. While the day goes by, the stars' brightness is worked out once a frame instead of twice. The Moonlight clouds, the Comet streamers and the eclipse corona do less work each frame.
- **Lighter night skies.** The Moonlight and Synthwave skies (their shapes, stars and the Synthwave sun's stripes), the Eclipse (its glow, milky way and black sun) and the Comet stay put where the lyrics face from one frame to the next instead of working out every corner again, and as the Moonlight clouds drift, repainting them only works out the clouds themselves, not the sky and moonlight behind them every time. They look the same.
- **Lighter bars, menus and cards.** The bar keeps its line laid out instead of measuring it again every frame, and the **Record card** keeps its times and cut titles. The settings window lays out each row once per frame instead of several times, and remembers the right-to-left text it has already put in order. A song library card without a cover works out its big letter once instead of every frame. Names cut short with "…" in the song library and the settings are cut once instead of every frame. Nothing looks different.
- **Less garbage each frame.** The World and Arc lyrics and the font checks make fewer throwaway objects each frame, so Java has less to clean up. The World words also keep the colours and letters they hand the game from one frame to the next, instead of making them anew for every copy of every word (its shadow, its outline by day, its letters), the Lines and Arc lyrics keep their colours from frame to frame, and the top bar lays out the note it shows for a song without a cover once instead of every frame. Nothing looks different.
- **Round shapes in fewer pieces.** The top bar's pill, its equaliser and signal bars and the round space for the cover, and the Record card's record, are drawn from about half as many pieces, so the game has fewer things to build and sort each frame. They look the same.

### Changed

- **Which lyrics are used.** The mod is stricter about which lyrics it shows and rechecks saved ones.
  - When the lyrics site (LRCLIB) doesn't have the song, the mod no longer shows lyrics from a different song, even one by the same artist, so such a song now shows none. A title with a translation or romanisation in brackets still finds its lyrics.
  - A copy of the lyrics whose song length is more than 20 seconds off your song's is no longer used (it was often another version's lyrics).
  - When the lyrics site's best match for a song has only plain lyrics, the mod also looks for a synced copy before settling for the plain one. A lyrics file with only tags and no lines no longer counts as an answer.
  - Lyrics saved by version 0.8.0 or older are checked again the next time you play the song. If the lyrics site has other lyrics for it, they replace the saved ones. If it has none, the saved ones stay for that play and are looked up fresh the next time.
- **Pauses and fades.** A line that is only "(Instrumental)", "(music)", "Instrumental", "♪ instrumental ♪", "(Intro)", "(Outro)", "(Solo)" or a note emoji now counts as a pause instead of being shown as words. A line that is just "Music" is still sung. A line starting with a part tag such as "[Chorus] words" or "[Verse 1: Someone] words" no longer shows the tag, in timed and untimed lyrics alike. In Lines and Arc, a line that ended more than a second and a half ago (the last lyric during the outro, or a line before a long instrumental part) fades out; in Lines the line above it fades with it, and so do the notes of a closing pause (lyrics that end with an empty line) and the last words above them.
- **At most three flashes a second.** When lines come very quickly, the glow, crosshair, hat and sky flashes no longer restart for every line: they start at most three times a second. Normal songs look the same.
- **Themes keep your other settings.** Picking a theme now changes only what themes set (the layout, colours, fonts, glow, size, opacity, animation, sky and a few more). Settings no theme touches, such as **Karaoke fill**, **Shadow** and **Two-tone**, stay as you set them, and the theme still shows as picked (not Custom).
- **Floating distance.** With Floating placement, every step of the **Distance** slider now moves the lyrics nearer or farther (before, 8 to 24 were all the same distance, and so were 96 to 160). They keep the same size on screen, so you see it as you walk past them or with **See through blocks** off. The default is unchanged.
- **Timing sliders.** The **Timing** and **This song** sliders now reach 5 seconds either way.
- **Spotify asks less.** With Spotify signed in, when the lyrics are off and none of the mod's screens is open, the mod asks Spotify for the song only every 15 seconds. When Spotify keeps failing, the mod waits longer each time before asking again, but no longer than 30 seconds (a Spotify app that doesn't know your account waits a minute). When Spotify says it is busy, the mod waits as long as Spotify asks (up to 5 minutes).
- **Clearer messages.** With no Client ID pasted, the Music tab now says "Paste your Client ID first" and no "can't read your music player" pop-up appears. The old "Spotify sign-in needs port" line goes away when you press **Sign in** or **Sign out**. The sign-in page opened in your browser reads right to left for Hebrew. A lyrics site that answers with an odd error shows "no lyrics" instead of blaming your internet. On a Mac, the "Nothing playing" bar in the settings no longer suggests browsers, and it stays quiet while the music player can't be read.
- **Settings texts and visibility.** Settings show only where they matter, and their texts say what they do.
  - The **Hide lyrics** card is now **Hide**, because its rows also hide the top bar, the **Record card** and the sky effects. The texts of **Karaoke fill** (it lights up the top bar's words too), **Top bar**, **Accent colour**, **Draw on top**, **Song name only on change**, **Hide in multiplayer**, **Show underground too** and **This song** now say what the setting really does. **Show underground too** only shows when **See through blocks** is off, since otherwise it changes nothing. **Depth** only shows in Arc, the one layout that draws it, and **Shadow** is hidden in Arc while **Depth** is on, since Depth replaces it there. The settings window's footer says just "Esc to close" when **Open settings** has no key, and the **Show or hide lyrics** key now says "Lyrics on" or "Lyrics off" above the hotbar. In a small window, the choices in a row of buttons (like the **Record card**'s corner) keep a gap between names instead of touching.
  - In the World layout, the settings it doesn't use (**Draw on top**, **Depth**, **Shadow**, **Pulse**, **Bigger current word**, and **Karaoke fill** while the top bar shows no lyrics) are hidden, as **Animation** already was. With Floating placement, **Distance** shows the real distance in blocks (for example "10.7 blocks" rather than "64 blocks"). **Strength** now shows when only **Constellations** is on, since it changes how bright they are, and **Sky speed** and **Pulse with the lyrics** show with **Constellations** and the other sky effects too. **Background** (how dark the bar is) also shows when only the Record card is on, since the card uses it.
  - The **Height** setting is hidden for Arc when it has no effect (Floating, or Direction Follow), but still found by search.
  - A sky **Strength** of 0 in the settings file now shows as 10%, where the slider starts. Pasted search text is cleaned up like typed text. A few English and Hebrew texts say what they mean (the previous line, **Preview**, **Aurora**).
  - The album picture is called "album cover" everywhere in the settings and help pages.
- **Reset all.** **Reset all** keeps your intro tour done, your update choice, your Spotify Client ID, your per-song timings and your recent searches.
- **Welcome tour and Hebrew texts.** The tour says which apps SkyLyrics can read on a Mac (Music and Spotify, not browsers), that macOS will ask for permission, and that signing in to Spotify is optional and needs Premium and a free developer app. On a Mac, the permission texts say "your launcher". The Music tab says "No Spotify or Music playing". The Hebrew texts speak in the plural, write Spotify and Minecraft in Hebrew letters, and say "no access" for the internet error. A few smoother lines (Draw on top, Karaoke fill, the Mac browser note).
- **Help pages.** The Troubleshooting page and FAQ now say what to expect with Replay Mod and Flashback recordings (the lyrics follow the music playing when you render, not when you recorded) and with Distant Horizons (which night skies can show in front of far-away terrain).
- **Game log.** The mod's lines in the game log no longer show song names or your home folder name, and a problem that repeats (offline, a failed save of the settings or the **Recently heard** list) is written once, so the log is safe to attach to a bug report.
